data.summary: The plan front‑loads Unit 3 (the student’s weak area) while introducing core concepts from Units 1 and 2. Subsequent weeks rotate through the remaining units, reinforcing earlier material and ending with mixed review and timed practice. Each week stays within the 15‑hour limit and includes the live class that matches the week’s topics.

tasks: Read textbook sections 1.1‑1.2 and 2.1‑2.2; take concise notes.
Do 12 free‑response problems on displacement, velocity, acceleration, and free‑body diagrams; check answers with the solution guide.
Create a one‑page summary sheet of key equations for kinematics and Newton’s second law.

weeks.focus: Work, energy, and conservation concepts (weak unit)
tasks: Watch the live class 10500 and take notes on work and energy conservation.
Complete the class worksheet (provided by the instructor) covering 3.2 and 3.4.
Solve 10 FRQs on work‑energy theorem and conservation of energy; grade with the scoring rubric.
Read sections on power (3.5) and linear momentum (4.1‑4.2).
Do 8 problems calculating power in various scenarios.
Do 8 impulse‑momentum problems; compare solutions to answer key.
Write a brief paragraph linking work‑energy concepts to momentum (for synthesis).
Read textbook chapters on rotational kinematics, torque, rotational kinetic energy, and angular momentum conservation.
Complete 6 problems on rotational kinematics (5.1) and 6 on torque (5.3).
Solve 6 FRQs on rotational kinetic energy (6.1) and angular momentum conservation (6.4).
Create a comparison table of linear vs. rotational dynamics equations.
Take a 60‑minute timed practice exam covering all units; use official AP practice test.
Review each incorrect answer, referencing notes and solution guides.
Do 5 free‑response questions from each of the listed topics for targeted reinforcement.
Update the master formula sheet with any missing equations discovered during review.

data.final_week_advice: In the last week, focus on exam strategy: practice pacing, eliminate answer choices quickly, and simulate test conditions. Review your formula sheet, and ensure you can explain each core concept in under a minute.
